areas.label: Text to URL-friendly slugs
areas.summary: The public slugify function chooses the compatibility pipeline by default. Callers can explicitly select the modern pipeline; the command-line entry point uses the same public function.

areas.label: Command-line input
areas.summary: Parses text or standard input and conversion options, translates arguments into public API parameters, and prints the resulting slug.

areas.label: Algorithm selection and modern conversion
areas.summary: Selects legacy or modern conversion. Modern helpers decode entities, transliterate text, preserve allowed Unicode characters, and enforce output length.

areas.label: Compatibility conversion
areas.summary: Preserves the legacy output pipeline, including replacement stages, transliteration, entity decoding, stopword removal, and optional smart truncation.

areas.label: Public exports
areas.summary: Re-exports conversion functions, special-character mappings, and package metadata.

areas.label: Behavior and compatibility checks
areas.summary: Checks legacy behavior, release regressions, command-line interruption, backend errors, combining marks, and modern word boundaries.

steps.note: The entry point parses arguments, builds keyword parameters, and prints the public slugify result.
Accept text arguments or standard input, validate replacement syntax, and reject simultaneous text and stdin.
Forward algorithm, backend, and replacement stage only when explicitly supplied, preserving API defaults.
The default algorithm is legacy. This branch delegates to the compatibility implementation in _legacy.py.
Normalize or transliterate, decode entities, clean characters, remove stopwords, and apply requested replacements.
Called only when max_length is positive; the caller then applies the requested separator and returns the slug.
Explicit algorithm='modern' selects this pipeline; it is not the default.
Validate length, separator, input type, backend, and replacement stage before transforming text.
Decode enabled named, decimal, and hexadecimal references before normalization.
On the ASCII-output branch, ASCII input returns immediately; other text uses the selected transliteration backend.
Alternative Unicode-output branch: retain letters, numbers, valid combining marks, and permitted joiners; replace other characters with separators.
After cleanup, stopwords, and replacements, enforce length using whole words or a hard cut, accounting for the requested separator.

limitations: Python call links resolve same-file lexical calls. Cross-file imports, external libraries, and dynamic dispatch may remain unresolved; inventory coverage is broader than call-resolution coverage.
Guided paths explain inspected source branches, not a recorded execution. The modern transliteration and Unicode-preservation steps are alternatives.
All tracked files and parsed Python declarations are included. Project code and dependencies were not executed.
